basil.store: Stems in a glass of water at room temperature: the fridge blackens it.
basil.preserve: Make pesto and freeze it in ice-cube trays.

parsley.store: Stems in water in the fridge for a week.
parsley.preserve: Chop and freeze, or blitz into a green sauce.
parsley.use: By the handful: tabbouleh, salsa verde, over everything.

coriander.store: Stems in water in the fridge for a few days.
coriander.preserve: Freeze chopped in oil; save the seeds when it bolts.
coriander.use: Leaves in curries and salsas; the seeds ground for spice.

chives.store: Snip as you need them; they wilt fast once cut.
chives.use: Over eggs, potatoes and soured cream; the flowers in salads.

mint.store: Stems in water in the fridge for a week.
mint.preserve: Make mint sauce, or dry the leaves for tea.
mint.use: With peas and new potatoes, or fresh mint tea.

rosemary.store: Pick as needed all year; it keeps a week in the fridge.

thyme.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
thyme.preserve: Dries well: hang small bunches somewhere airy.
thyme.use: In stews, with mushrooms, and on roast chicken.

sage.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
sage.preserve: Dry the leaves, or fry them crisp and keep in a jar for a few days.
sage.use: Fried in butter with squash or pasta.

dill.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
dill.preserve: Freeze chopped; save the seeds for pickling.

oregano.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
oregano.preserve: Dries better than almost any herb.

fennel.store: Fronds in water in the fridge for a few days.
fennel.preserve: Dry the seeds when they turn brown.
fennel.use: Fronds with fish; seeds in bread and sausages.

lemon-balm.store: Stems in water for a few days.
lemon-balm.use: Fresh in tea, or with fruit.

bay.preserve: Dry the leaves flat for a fortnight.
bay.use: In stocks, stews and rice pudding.

tarragon.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
tarragon.preserve: Keep sprigs in white wine vinegar.

sorrel.store: In a bag in the fridge for a day or two.
sorrel.preserve: Cook to a purée and freeze.
sorrel.use: Lemony leaves in salads, or a sauce for fish.

lovage.store: In the fridge for a few days.
lovage.use: A little goes a long way: like celery, in soups and stocks.

horseradish.store: Lift roots as needed, or keep in damp sand.
horseradish.preserve: Grate into vinegar, or make horseradish sauce.
horseradish.use: Grated fresh with roast beef or smoked fish. Grate it by an open window.

salad-burnet.store: Pick as needed: it wilts fast.
salad-burnet.use: Cucumber-flavoured leaves in salads and drinks.

chervil.store: In a bag in the fridge for a couple of days.
chervil.use: Gently aniseed: with eggs and fish.

chamomile.store: Dry the flowers soon after picking.
chamomile.preserve: Dried in a jar for a year.

marjoram.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
marjoram.use: Gentler than oregano: with tomatoes and lamb.

winter-savory.store: Pick as needed, even in winter.

hyssop.use: A little, minty and bitter, with fatty meat or in tea.

lemon-verbena.preserve: Dry the leaves: they keep their scent.
lemon-verbena.use: Tea, or steeped in cream for ice cream.

lemongrass.store: Stalks in the fridge for a couple of weeks.
lemongrass.use: Bruised into curries, soups and tea.

shiso.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
